nodes.label: COSC3500 Milestone 1 / Milestone 2 Specification
nodes.rationale: Personalized spec (dated July 30, 2026) issued for a single student; sharing the document is a misconduct penalty. Defines one shared rubric for both milestone presentations.

nodes.label: Milestone 1 (Serial Presentation)
nodes.rationale: Video-only deliverable, no in-person interview; likely less to talk about than Milestone 2, so shorter presentations are acceptable.

nodes.label: Milestone 2 (Parallel Presentation)
nodes.rationale: Adds an identity-verified in-person interview scheduled in the second week of exams (the week after the video submission is due). Using every parallel technique is not required; a single technique analysed thoroughly can earn an excellent mark.

nodes.label: Shared Marking Rubric
nodes.rationale: The same basic rubric is used for both the Serial (Milestone 1) and Parallel (Milestone 2) presentations so feedback from Milestone 1 can be applied directly to Milestone 2.

nodes.label: 10-Minute Video Presentation
nodes.rationale: Strict 10-minute maximum; assessors stop watching after 10 minutes. Quality over duration: a shorter high-quality presentation beats a longer low-quality one; time allocation across topics is a strategic choice since different models need different amounts of background. Multiple takes and splicing are allowed but the face must remain visible throughout.

nodes.label: Identity Verification (pass/fail)
nodes.rationale: The presentation doubles as identity-verified assessment: the student's face must be visible in the presentation, and abrupt head movement across splices is tolerated since the face is only checked for identity.

nodes.label: In-Person Interview (Milestone 2 only, pass/fail)
nodes.rationale: Identity-verified hurdle: approximately 7 minutes long, held in the second week of exams (the week after the Milestone 2 video is due); must be passed to pass Milestone 2 and hence the course. Milestone 1 has no interview.

nodes.label: Introduction and Background (20%)
nodes.rationale: Brings assessors up to speed on the simulated model; each presentation must be self-contained because assessors will likely not remember Milestone 1 when watching Milestone 2. Overlap between milestones is expected.

nodes.label: Optimisation (25%)
nodes.rationale: Covers optimisations attempted and their performance, techniques tried that failed or were considered and rejected, how the problem was structured and/or parallelised (Milestone 2) for speed, and trade-offs made.

nodes.label: Benchmarking (25%)
nodes.rationale: Benchmark setup must avoid inaccurate/misleading results; discussion should cover Amdahl's law and Gustafson's law (Milestone 2), hotspot and bottleneck identification, and how performance scales with problem size. Benchmarks must run on at least one of the UQ clusters.

nodes.label: Presentation (20%)
nodes.rationale: Assesses conveying results via visual and verbal presentation: choice of topics and time allocated to each, verbal delivery, slide design, and data visualisation/representation.

nodes.label: Reflection/Conclusion (10%)
nodes.rationale: Summarise main conclusions: what was learnt or most surprising, what would be done differently, how the work would be extended with more time; for Milestone 1, plans for Milestone 2.

nodes.label: Code Submission (pass/fail)
nodes.rationale: Well-commented source code plus associated files (Makefiles, slurm scripts) needed to compile and check the code. Not directly assessed; required to verify the presented models were actually implemented and as reference for assessors.

nodes.label: Submission Format (pass/fail)
nodes.rationale: Video must be H.264 and under 100MB because that is Blackboard's file upload limit (~1 Mbit/s bitrate). Naming: Milestone{#milestone number}_48008361.mp4 (e.g. Milestone1_48008361.mp4); code and video submitted as a single combined .zip with the same naming convention (e.g. Milestone1_48008361.zip).

nodes.label: Parallel Implementation
nodes.rationale: Multiple paths to a good final result: a single technique (AVX, OpenMP, MPI, or CUDA) analysed very thoroughly, comparisons of technologies (CPU vs GPU), or combinations (OpenMP+MPI). OpenMP in isolation is the least common path to an excellent mark but has been achieved.

nodes.label: CPU vs GPU Comparison Approach
nodes.rationale: Common Milestone 2 approach: it is easier to first implement and verify the parallel model on CPU before progressing to a scaled-up GPU implementation. Since a GPU is much faster than a CPU, parallelised CPU code can appropriately support the GPU for once-off routines at the start/finish of the simulation that are too difficult or tedious for GPU but still computationally intensive enough to warrant an optimised CPU implementation.

nodes.label: Heston PDE (2-D stock x variance grid)
nodes.rationale: Price one European option by filling a 2-D grid of what-if scenarios backwards in time from expiry; 3x3 stencil whose diagonal entries carry the price/vol correlation.
nodes.norm_label: heston pde (2-d stock x variance grid)

nodes.label: Explicit Euler + central differences scheme
nodes.rationale: Simplest correct scheme; its conditional stability makes the stability boundary itself a deliverable.

nodes.label: Flat row-major grid idx = j*Ns + i
nodes.rationale: Inner loop walks contiguous memory and sets up SIMD/OpenMP for Milestone 2.
nodes.norm_label: flat row-major grid idx = j*ns + i

nodes.label: Two buffers with pointer swap per step
nodes.rationale: cur read-only, next write-only; avoids half-read sheets and avoids copying the grid each step.
nodes.norm_label: two buffers with pointer swap per step

nodes.label: v=0 degenerate transport boundary
nodes.rationale: Diffusion vanishes at v=0 and drift kappa*theta points inward, so solve the reduced PDE with upwind v-difference; Dirichlet over-determines and central-v needs a meaningless ghost point (in't Hout and Foulon treatment).

nodes.label: Feller condition check (2 kappa theta >= xi^2)
nodes.rationale: Reference params marginally violate it (0.1200 < 0.1225); scheme stays valid, uniform v-grid slightly under-resolves near v=0, stated as a known limitation.
nodes.norm_label: feller condition check (2 kappa theta >= xi^2)

nodes.norm_label: s=0, s=smax and v=vmax neumann boundaries

nodes.label: Explicit stability estimate dt_stable
nodes.rationale: Reported by the solver to enable the instability demo; the bound binds at the high-v/high-S corner where the checkerboard erupts first.

nodes.label: Cell-updates per second metric
nodes.rationale: A rate comparable across grid sizes, timed with steady_clock around the time loop only, so a short-nt run measures the same throughput as a long one.

nodes.label: OOP-shaped modern C++, memory-safe code style
nodes.rationale: Author knows Python OOP and is learning C++; Grid class with private fields, abstract Solver base, Config/SolveResult structs, unique_ptr factory, no raw new/delete so leaks and double-frees are unrepresentable.
nodes.norm_label: oop-shaped modern c++, memory-safe code style

nodes.label: Narration comments rule
nodes.rationale: Each optimisation, boundary site and non-obvious decision gets a one-line plain-English label, as teaching aids for the video and interview prep.

nodes.label: Working agreement: learning by building
nodes.rationale: Explain before code, author-writes list, checkpoint quizzes, STUDY_GUIDE kept in sync; step_level1 reservation waived in P7 on condition the kernels are well commented.

nodes.label: heston CLI contract and CSV output
nodes.rationale: Fixed early so scripts can be written against it; controls labelled opt-ctl-order/opt-ctl-branch so a CSV row cannot be misread as the ladder continuing.
nodes.norm_label: heston cli contract and csv output

nodes.label: Ablation ladder --opt-level 0..6
nodes.rationale: Cumulative ladder where each rung adds exactly one technique, re-runnable by markers in one sbatch sweep; duplication accepted because diffing adjacent kernels shows one technique.

nodes.label: Level 1: loop-invariant hoisting + lookup table + CSE
nodes.norm_label: level 1: loop-invariant hoisting + lookup table + cse

nodes.label: Level 2: strength reduction (reciprocals instead of divides)
nodes.rationale: Division throughput 5-14 cycles vs 0-1 for multiply; first rung whose last bits move.
nodes.norm_label: level 2: strength reduction (reciprocals instead of divides)

nodes.label: Level 3: cache-friendly loop order
nodes.rationale: Null by construction because the baseline already loops outer-j inner-i.

nodes.label: Level 4: hoist conditionals / loop splitting
nodes.rationale: Null by construction because the baseline already peels the v=0 row.

nodes.label: Negative controls ctl-order and ctl-branch
nodes.rationale: Levels 3 and 4 cannot recover a loss that never happened, so build the wrong version from level 5 and time it to give those techniques a number.

nodes.label: Floating-point contract across the ladder
nodes.rationale: Levels 0-1 bit-identical to baseline (max_abs_diff == 0.0); levels 2-8 within measured per-quantity relative tolerance (worst 3.3e-15, tolerance 1e-11).

nodes.label: Dispatch kernel once outside the time loop
nodes.rationale: Per-cell level checks would poison the very timings the ladder exists to measure.
nodes.norm_label: dispatch kernel once outside the time loop

nodes.label: reference.cfg NaN failure and fix (nt=980000, v_max=0.64)
nodes.rationale: nt=2000 was 527x over the stability bound and printed nan; criterion recorded as passed at P2 but never actually run. Fixed in P7, giving 196.1684 vs Fourier 196.1692 (4.2e-6).
nodes.norm_label: reference.cfg nan failure and fix (nt=980000, v_max=0.64)

nodes.label: Benchmark protocol (rangpur compute node, pinned, 5 sweeps)
nodes.rationale: --exclusive and --nodelist=r730-2 because the partition mixes hardware; 15-minute QOS forces five sweeps; make test runs before every bench job; consume results; problem must not fit in cache.
nodes.norm_label: benchmark protocol (rangpur compute node, pinned, 5 sweeps)

nodes.label: Equal-work grid sweep (nt and maturity scaled per grid)
nodes.rationale: Keeps dt <= 0.7 dt_stable and ~4e8 cell updates on every grid; legitimate because the metric is a rate, verified by diag_denormal.
nodes.norm_label: equal-work grid sweep (nt and maturity scaled per grid)

nodes.label: Page-size trap (huge pages vs 4 KiB, 1.66x)
nodes.rationale: Rep 1 is mmap-backed with transparent huge pages; glibc raises the mmap threshold so later reps reuse heap on 4 KiB pages and blow the TLB. Proved by pinning MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_; sweep E re-measures with it pinned.

nodes.label: Milestone 2 SIMD via AVX intrinsics
nodes.rationale: Kernel measured compute-bound, so widening arithmetic is the right next move; expect closer to vector width than L04's ~4x rule of thumb.

nodes.label: Milestone 2 OpenMP on outer j loop
nodes.rationale: Zero synchronisation inside a step since threads read immutable cur and write disjoint rows of next; never critical in the hot loop.
nodes.norm_label: milestone 2 openmp on outer j loop

nodes.rationale: Avoid facts drifting apart: scheme and style in PLAN.md, cluster ops in RUNNING.md, numbers in RESULTS.md, explanation in WALKTHROUGH.md and STUDY_GUIDE.md; everything else links.

nodes.label: Headline: only one of six techniques did anything
nodes.rationale: The point is not the ~2.5x speedup but that the only effective technique was the one the compiler is forbidden to perform itself (reciprocal substitution changes results).

nodes.label: Finding: worthwhile hand optimisations are ones -O2 is forbidden to do
nodes.rationale: Replacing x/(2ds) with x*(1/(2ds)) changes last bits and -ffast-math is off, so GCC cannot do it; every other rung GCC 8.5 already performed.

nodes.label: Negative controls ctl-order (2.1x) and ctl-branch (1.0x)

nodes.rationale: GCC 8.5 does not enable the tree vectoriser at -O2, so disabling it measured nothing.

nodes.label: Roofline analysis (compute-bound, 82% of scalar peak)
nodes.rationale: Disproved the memory-bound assumption; baseline is division-bound, L6 compute-bound, so the next win is SIMD.

nodes.label: Huge-page effect (1.66x from 2 MiB THP)
nodes.rationale: glibc dynamic mmap threshold gave rep 1 huge pages and reps 2-5 not, so medians averaged two regimes; fixed by pinning MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_.

nodes.label: SIMD (Single Instruction Multiple Data)
nodes.rationale: All lanes run in lockstep on one instruction, managed in hardware; ideal for applying the same op to large arrays, 4-8x speedups realistic

nodes.label: MIMD / Multi-threading
nodes.rationale: Threads managed by OS, not synchronised, can run different instructions; SIMD can be layered on top of it for further speedup

nodes.label: AVX (256-bit, 8 float32 / 4 float64)
nodes.rationale: Focus of lecture: widely supported, float-first; principles transfer to SSE and AVX-512

nodes.label: FMA3 instruction set
nodes.rationale: Named for 3 operands, not a version number

nodes.label: Compiler auto-vectorisation (-O3 / /O2)
nodes.rationale: Limited: O2 scalar loop was 11x slower than intrinsic version, so compiler failed to vectorise a simple sum

nodes.label: Manual loop unrolling for vectorisation
nodes.rationale: Still gives subpar results; compiler struggles to vectorise

nodes.label: Intrinsic functions
nodes.rationale: Pick the exact vector instruction, compiler handles registers and loads; most of assembly's gain without its cost

nodes.label: Hand-written assembly
nodes.rationale: Marginal additional benefit over intrinsics for much more effort

nodes.label: __m256 / __m256d / __m256i vector types
nodes.rationale: One integer type shared by all int widths; separate float and double types

nodes.label: Accidental AVX-512 intrinsic crash pitfall
nodes.rationale: Some AVX-512 intrinsics start with _mm256; MSVC compiles them anyway and the binary crashes on CPUs without AVX-512; include narrower headers to avoid

nodes.label: Aligned memory allocation (aligned_alloc to 32/64 bytes)
nodes.rationale: Align to 64-byte cache line so a vector never straddles two cache lines; unaligned penalty mostly gone on modern CPUs

nodes.label: Instruction latency vs throughput (CPI)
nodes.rationale: Latency is pipeline length, throughput is pipe width; CPI below 1 from superscalar execution

nodes.label: Division is expensive, prefer multiply
nodes.rationale: Division throughput ~10x worse and latency 3-5x worse than multiply; reformulate as multiplication by reciprocal where possible

nodes.label: Fused multiply-add (_mm256_fmadd_ps)
nodes.rationale: Two flops in the time of one, and a single rounding error instead of two

nodes.label: Memory-bound vs compute-bound limit
nodes.rationale: FMA every cycle needs ~4.6 TB/s for 8 cores vs ~115 GB/s DRAM; replacing mul+add with FMA may give no speedup if memory bound

nodes.label: Vector sqrt and fast approximate rsqrt
nodes.rationale: rsqrt not IEEE-754 exact but ~3x latency and ~6x throughput gain
nodes.norm_label: vector sqrt and fast approximate rsqrt

nodes.label: Aligned/unaligned load and store intrinsics
nodes.rationale: Lecturer instead aliases aligned arrays as __m256 arrays; compiler inserts loads

nodes.label: Ordered/unordered and signalling NaN comparison flags
nodes.norm_label: ordered/unordered and signalling nan comparison flags

nodes.label: Branchless if/else via mask and/andnot/or
nodes.rationale: SIMD cannot branch; compute both branches and merge with masks, wasting idle lanes

nodes.label: 128-bit lane restriction of AVX permutes
nodes.rationale: Original AVX was two 128-bit SSE units strapped together; in-lane permute is cheaper (latency 1 vs 3) but cannot cross lanes

nodes.label: Gather (AVX2) / scatter (AVX-512)
nodes.rationale: Flexible indexed loads but relatively slow (latency ~17)

nodes.label: Horizontal reduction of a vector accumulator
nodes.rationale: After vector loop the 8 partial sums still need summing: hadd twice, lane-swap permute, add
nodes.norm_label: horizontal reduction of a vector accumulator

nodes.label: set / set1 pseudo-intrinsics
nodes.rationale: Map to several instructions; set takes elements right to left

nodes.label: Remainder (tail) loop for N not multiple of vector width
nodes.norm_label: remainder (tail) loop for n not multiple of vector width

nodes.label: Complex dot-product AVX demo
nodes.rationale: 2^26 floats so data exceeds cache; interleaved re/im; got ~4x over optimised scalar

nodes.label: Parallel reduction in CUDA
nodes.rationale: Reduction needs threads to communicate; built up in versions v1-v4 on integral-under-curve example

nodes.label: Mark Harris NVIDIA 'Optimizing Parallel Reduction' slides
nodes.rationale: Partly outdated since Volta (warp-synchronous unrolling no longer safe)
nodes.norm_label: mark harris nvidia 'optimizing parallel reduction' slides

nodes.label: Single-thread kernel is far slower than CPU
nodes.rationale: GPUs are bad at serial work; <<<1,1>>> took ~20000 us
nodes.norm_label: single-thread kernel is far slower than cpu

nodes.label: CUDA_CHECK error macro (do-while(false), __FILE__/__LINE__)
nodes.rationale: do-while(false) makes the macro behave syntactically like a function; prints cudaGetErrorString and aborts

nodes.label: cudaMalloc / cudaMemcpy / cudaFree
nodes.rationale: Allocate before timing so benchmarks measure kernel only; use sizeof(element) to survive type changes

nodes.label: v1 single-block tree reduction (~245 us)
nodes.rationale: Inter-block communication can deadlock when grid exceeds resident blocks, so reduce within a block first

nodes.label: Sequential addressing (halving stride, tid < i)
nodes.rationale: Keeps active threads contiguous so whole warps retire, avoids divergence and shared-memory bank conflicts

nodes.label: __syncthreads inside conditional deadlocks
nodes.rationale: Every thread in the block must reach the barrier

nodes.label: Read-after-write race between threads without barrier
nodes.rationale: v1 gave wrong result until __syncthreads was added
nodes.norm_label: read-after-write race between threads without barrier

nodes.label: v2 multi-block reduction with repeated kernel launches (~100 us)
nodes.norm_label: v2 multi-block reduction with repeated kernel launches (~100 us)

nodes.label: Global index blockDim.x*blockIdx.x+threadIdx.x
nodes.rationale: Bug in v2 was starting the loop at threadIdx instead of global index

nodes.label: Ping-pong buffer pointer swap between launches
nodes.norm_label: ping-pong buffer pointer swap between launches

nodes.label: Default-stream kernel ordering (implicit sync)
nodes.rationale: Kernels in the same stream run in order, so no explicit cudaDeviceSynchronize between reduction passes

nodes.label: Keep sub-buffer offsets 256-bit aligned
nodes.rationale: cudaMalloc returns aligned memory; offset into it rounded up to multiple of 4 doubles, required for later vectorised loads

nodes.label: __shared__ memory (static and extern dynamic)
nodes.rationale: Per-block scratch carved from L1, much faster than global; dynamic size passed as third launch parameter

nodes.label: Shared-memory bank conflicts (32 banks)
nodes.rationale: Different addresses in same bank within a warp serialise; consecutive access avoids it

nodes.label: cudaDeviceSetSharedMemConfig 8-byte banks
nodes.rationale: Default bank width 32 bits; 8-byte banks suit doubles, no visible change here

nodes.label: Interleaved addressing leaves warps mostly idle
nodes.norm_label: interleaved addressing leaves warps mostly idle

nodes.label: v4 vectorised double4 loads (~60-70 us)
nodes.rationale: reinterpret_cast to double4/float4 for 128-bit fetches; needs const pointer and alignment

nodes.label: Tail handling with switch fall-through for N%4
nodes.rationale: Validated by rerunning with N not a multiple of 4
nodes.norm_label: tail handling with switch fall-through for n%4

nodes.label: Volta independent thread scheduling (CC 7.0)
nodes.rationale: Threads in a warp may diverge, so warp-synchronous code without sync is unsafe

nodes.label: Cooperative groups (incl. grid-wide sync)
nodes.rationale: Can reduce to a single kernel launch

nodes.label: Rangpur GPU node with module cuda/11.4
nodes.norm_label: rangpur gpu node with module cuda/11.4

nodes.label: OpenMP
nodes.rationale: Compiler add-on (pragmas) for C/C++/Fortran MIMD parallelism; core features stable since v1/v2; designed to add parallelism progressively to an existing serial program

nodes.label: Race condition
nodes.rationale: Program outcome changes with thread scheduling; one C line (sum += f) is load/add/store so concurrent writes lose updates; formally undefined behaviour (invalid code)

nodes.label: Synchronization
nodes.rationale: Prevents data conflicts but is expensive (threads block like a crowd through one door); design programs to minimise synchronization

nodes.label: omp_get_num_threads()
nodes.rationale: Always query actual thread count inside the region; OpenMP may not give the number requested

nodes.label: OMP_NUM_THREADS environment variable
nodes.rationale: Main practical way to set thread count at runtime from the shell (e.g. in a slurm script) without recompiling

nodes.label: omp_get_max_threads()
nodes.rationale: Upper bound on threads in a region; use to size per-thread arrays

nodes.label: Numerical integration of 1/(1+x^2) = pi/4 (pi_serial.cpp)
nodes.rationale: Midpoint-rule benchmark with known exact answer so parallel correctness can be verified against the serial result

nodes.label: #pragma omp for (worksharing loop)
nodes.rationale: OpenMP does the start/end bookkeeping that the manual block decomposition does by hand

nodes.label: #pragma omp critical
nodes.rationale: Only one thread runs the statement at a time; correct but inside a hot loop it serialises and adds lock overhead (lecture demo ran ~40x slower than serial)

nodes.label: Thread-local partial sum then single critical combine
nodes.rationale: Removes synchronization from the loop body; contention happens once per thread at the end (about 4x on a 4-core laptop)
nodes.norm_label: thread-local partial sum then single critical combine

nodes.label: Non-deterministic floating-point result
nodes.rationale: Floating-point addition is not associative ((a+b)+c != a+(b+c)), so summation order from thread scheduling changes the low bits; algorithms must be robust so this error stays small (~1e-12)

nodes.label: reduction clause
nodes.rationale: Built-in equivalent of local partial sums plus critical combine; makes parallelising a serial accumulation a one-line addition

nodes.label: Variable scoping (shared by default)
nodes.rationale: Outer-scope variables are shared in parallel regions by default, which is dangerous; prefer declaring locals inside the region

nodes.label: default(none) clause
nodes.rationale: Compiler forces explicit shared/private for every referenced variable, catching accidental sharing

nodes.label: private clause
nodes.rationale: Each thread gets a copy that is undefined on entry; little reason to use it over a block-local variable

nodes.label: const variable sharing compatibility (OpenMP 4.0 / GCC 9)
nodes.rationale: Older OpenMP implicitly shared const variables even with default(none) and erred if listed; since OpenMP 4.0 / GCC 9 they must be listed in shared

nodes.label: #pragma omp barrier
nodes.rationale: All threads reach this point before any proceed; needed when step 2 reads arrays written in step 1

nodes.label: Implicit barrier at end of worksharing loop
nodes.norm_label: implicit barrier at end of worksharing loop

nodes.label: nowait clause
nodes.rationale: Removes the implicit barrier when following work does not depend on the loop's results

nodes.label: #pragma omp master
nodes.rationale: Block run only by thread 0, no implicit barrier, so usually paired with an explicit barrier

nodes.label: #pragma omp single
nodes.rationale: Block run by whichever thread arrives first, with implicit barrier at end (removable with nowait); generally preferred over master

nodes.label: exchange_boundaries() serial step in parallel region
nodes.rationale: Grid/PDE pattern: threads update their blocks in parallel, then boundary data is exchanged serially by one thread before the next step
nodes.norm_label: exchange_boundaries() serial step in parallel region

nodes.label: Parallelize outermost loops first
nodes.rationale: Outer-loop parallelism gives larger work per thread and fewer fork/join and barrier costs than parallelising inner loops; target the hotspot that takes the most CPU time

nodes.label: Hyper-threading limits FP-bound speedup
nodes.rationale: Two hardware threads on one core compete for the same FP unit, so FP-heavy code scales with physical cores (4x on 4 cores/8 threads); HPC clusters often disable hyper-threading so each thread owns a full core

nodes.label: Thread oversubscription
nodes.rationale: More threads than hardware is allowed but extra threads block; most programs slow down from scattered memory access and cache misses (lecture saw an anomalous speedup at 40 threads)

nodes.label: Pragmas ignored without OpenMP (serial fallback)
nodes.rationale: A program using only directives (no omp.h API calls) still compiles as valid serial code when OpenMP is off; calling API functions requires including omp.h

nodes.label: Interleaved printf / IO across threads
nodes.rationale: Each printf is atomic but consecutive printf calls from different threads interleave; file output (e.g. grid dumps) must be scheduled deliberately to stay valid

nodes.label: Critical section in loop: 21 s parallel vs 0.5 s serial
nodes.rationale: Every iteration funnels 8 threads through one lock; synchronization overhead makes it far slower than serial, not just equal to it
nodes.norm_label: critical section in loop: 21 s parallel vs 0.5 s serial

nodes.label: macOS default clang lacks OpenMP (use Homebrew GCC)
nodes.rationale: Apple clang does not ship OpenMP support; tutor installs GCC via Homebrew to compile with -fopenmp on a Mac
nodes.norm_label: macos default clang lacks openmp (use homebrew gcc)

nodes.label: omp_set_dynamic()
nodes.rationale: Lets the runtime pick fewer threads than requested based on load (asked 16, got 7)

nodes.label: Requesting more threads than OS limit errors
nodes.norm_label: requesting more threads than os limit errors

nodes.label: schedule(static)
nodes.rationale: Default; consecutive equal chunks assigned up front; low overhead but threads finishing at different rates leave others idle

nodes.label: schedule(dynamic)
nodes.rationale: Threads grab chunks as they become free; balances uneven work at runtime cost

nodes.label: Schedule chunk size
nodes.rationale: Chunk size that does not match iterations/threads leaves threads idle (4 iterations, chunk 2, 4 threads: 2 idle)

nodes.label: collapse(n) clause
nodes.rationale: By default only the outer loop of a nest is split; collapse fuses independent nested loops into one iteration space so more work can be distributed; only valid when loops are independent

nodes.label: #pragma omp atomic (update/read/write)
nodes.rationale: Narrower than critical, protects a single memory update; can be faster, but partial sums or reduction remain better

nodes.label: firstprivate clause
nodes.rationale: Private copy initialised from the value outside the region, fixing uninitialised private variables

nodes.label: lastprivate clause
nodes.rationale: Copies the value from the sequentially last iteration back out; must be put on the for construct, not the parallel region

nodes.label: Shared loop counters race in parallel region
nodes.rationale: Outer-declared i,j shared by all threads cause skipped/duplicated iterations; making them private duplicates work rather than splitting it unless omp for is used
nodes.norm_label: shared loop counters race in parallel region

nodes.label: #pragma omp sections / section
nodes.rationale: Task parallelism for independent code blocks without a loop; threads beyond the number of sections sit idle

nodes.label: OpenMP simd directive (parallel for simd)
nodes.rationale: Hints the compiler to vectorise the threaded loop; speedup was inconsistent between machines/compilers, so it must be measured

nodes.label: Integration benchmark: 561 ms serial to 71 ms on 8 threads
nodes.rationale: 100 million steps; local sum + critical gave ~8x on 8 threads; reduction version same speed with fewer lines
nodes.norm_label: integration benchmark: 561 ms serial to 71 ms on 8 threads

nodes.label: Monte Carlo estimation of pi and e
nodes.rationale: Parallelised with parallel region + omp for + reduction on counts; ~4-5x on 8 threads (3 s to 0.75 s at 1e8 samples)
nodes.norm_label: monte carlo estimation of pi and e

nodes.label: thread_local random number generator
nodes.rationale: A shared RNG is a subtle race: threads may draw identical streams, biasing Monte Carlo; C++ thread_local gives each thread its own generator

nodes.label: Parallel overhead dominates for small problem sizes
nodes.rationale: Spawning threads and synchronising costs time, so small N may see no speedup; speedup also below thread count due to serial parts of the code
nodes.norm_label: parallel overhead dominates for small problem sizes

nodes.label: Message Passing Interface (MPI)
nodes.rationale: Specification with multiple implementations; library with C and Fortran bindings; portable distributed-memory parallelism replacing incompatible 1980s tools

nodes.label: SPMD model (Single Program, Multiple Data)
nodes.rationale: Multiple copies of one program in separate address spaces communicating only by messages; no shared variables, every variable is local to a process

nodes.label: MPI standard versions (MPI-1 to MPI-4)
nodes.rationale: MPI-1 1994 basic point-to-point; MPI-2 process spawn; MPI-3 non-blocking collectives and one-sided; MPI-4 64-bit counts, better hybrid OpenMP/CUDA support

nodes.label: Hybrid distributed memory (MPI + OpenMP)
nodes.rationale: Modern nodes are multicore; options are one MPI process per CPU (MPI uses shared memory within a node) or one process per node spawning OpenMP threads; programming model stays distributed memory

nodes.label: MPI communicator and rank
nodes.rationale: Collection of processes that may communicate; ranks 0..N-1 within a communicator

nodes.label: MPI_Send / MPI_Recv point-to-point
nodes.rationale: Every send must be matched by a receive on the destination; buffer must be contiguous; count is elements not bytes

nodes.label: MPI message tag
nodes.rationale: Identifier to distinguish multiple message streams; receive tag must match send tag (or MPI_ANY_TAG)

nodes.label: MPI datatypes (MPI_INT, MPI_DOUBLE, ...)
nodes.rationale: Originally for heterogeneous hardware conversion; user-defined datatypes can describe non-contiguous layouts and avoid packing copies

nodes.label: Message passing ring example
nodes.rationale: Inefficient: only one message in flight, N-1 processes blocked waiting at any moment

nodes.label: Dynamic size buffers (MPI_Get_count, MPI_Probe)
nodes.rationale: Receive into max-size buffer then query count, or Probe to size buffer before Recv; avoids a second size message

nodes.label: MPI_Send buffering semantics
nodes.rationale: MPI_Send may block or buffer internally; after return the send buffer is reusable; small messages often buffered, large ones block until matched

nodes.label: MPI_Ssend (synchronous send)
nodes.rationale: Blocks until matching receive posted; also acts as synchronisation

nodes.label: MPI_Bsend (buffered send)
nodes.rationale: Copies into user buffer via MPI_Buffer_attach; lecturer advises not to use

nodes.label: Non-blocking communication (MPI_Isend / MPI_Irecv)
nodes.rationale: Returns immediately with MPI_Request; buffer must not be touched until MPI_Wait/MPI_Test completes; any send kind matches any receive kind

nodes.label: Overlapping communication and computation
nodes.rationale: Post Irecv, do work and send, then Wait; lets all ranks send simultaneously instead of serialising like the blocking ring

nodes.label: Collective communication
nodes.rationale: Involves all processes in a communicator; more convenient than point-to-point and may be faster on specialised network hardware; implies a synchronisation point

nodes.label: MPI_Bcast (broadcast)
nodes.rationale: One root sends same data to all; used for config parameters, matrix-vector vector, avoiding many processes reading the same file

nodes.label: MPI_Scatter / MPI_Scatterv
nodes.rationale: Distributes chunks of an array from root; send_count is per process; Scatterv for uneven counts

nodes.label: MPI_Gather
nodes.rationale: Collects chunks at root; recv_count is per process not total; only root needs a valid receive buffer

nodes.label: MPI_Allgather
nodes.rationale: Gather followed by Bcast; implies N^2 style communication, benefits from fancy network hardware

nodes.label: MPI_Reduce
nodes.rationale: Apply an operation such as sum across all ranks to a root, like OpenMP reduction

nodes.label: MPI_Allreduce
nodes.rationale: Reduce followed by Bcast; every rank receives the result

nodes.label: Running MPI batch jobs via Slurm (sbatch)
nodes.rationale: Never run large compute jobs on the front-end login node; it slows every user and is not the target hardware; use job scripts with #SBATCH directives
nodes.norm_label: running mpi batch jobs via slurm (sbatch)

nodes.label: Slurm resource options (-N nodes, -n ntasks, -c cpus-per-task, --mem)
nodes.rationale: Tasks map to MPI ranks; -c is for OpenMP threads; memory per node or per CPU
nodes.norm_label: slurm resource options (-n nodes, -n ntasks, -c cpus-per-task, --mem)

nodes.label: mpiexec / mpirun launcher
nodes.rationale: mpiexec is the standard-defined launcher; mpirun is common but non-standard; inside a job script it picks up ntasks automatically

nodes.label: Open MPI implementation (openmpi3_eth module)
nodes.rationale: Most common open-source MPI implementation; not to be confused with OpenMP; getafix ethernet-only produces harmless high-speed-network warnings

nodes.label: mpic++ compiler wrapper
nodes.rationale: Wrapper around g++ that supplies MPI include and link flags

nodes.label: MPI errors fatal by default
nodes.rationale: Communication errors terminate the program by default, so examples skip checking return codes and status

nodes.label: Non-blocking progress pitfall (communication only inside MPI_Wait/MPI_Test)
nodes.rationale: Standard does not mandate asynchronous progress; older implementations did all communication inside Wait/Test giving no overlap benefit; modern ones use a private progress thread
nodes.norm_label: non-blocking progress pitfall (communication only inside mpi_wait/mpi_test)

nodes.label: Asymmetric pattern: one side non-blocking, other blocking
nodes.rationale: Usually unusual for both send and receive to be non-blocking; with blocking receive and Isend the send must be posted before the receive
nodes.norm_label: asymmetric pattern: one side non-blocking, other blocking

nodes.label: Root-symmetric collective code idiom
nodes.rationale: Write broadcast code so the root runs the same lines (resize is a no-op on root), avoiding if(rank!=root) branches

nodes.label: Single reader then broadcast for file I/O
nodes.rationale: Only one process reads input files then broadcasts; avoids multiplied disk I/O when all ranks hit the same file
nodes.norm_label: single reader then broadcast for file i/o

nodes.label: Custom sub-communicators
nodes.rationale: Rarely needed; main use is running collectives on a subset of processes

nodes.label: Node/task placement controls shared-memory vs network messaging
nodes.rationale: N nodes with 1 task per node forces network communication; many tasks on one node lets MPI use shared memory copies
nodes.norm_label: node/task placement controls shared-memory vs network messaging

nodes.label: Unspecified output ordering across ranks
nodes.rationale: Terminal output interleaving across processes is not specified by MPI; within one process order is preserved

nodes.label: Broadcast size then data for dynamic arrays
nodes.rationale: No facility to broadcast dynamic arrays directly; broadcast length, resize, then broadcast contents (std::string data() modifiable in C++17)
nodes.norm_label: broadcast size then data for dynamic arrays

nodes.label: Numerical integration of 1/(1+x^2) = pi/4 example
nodes.rationale: Known analytic answer gives a correctness check against the serial reference and allows timing comparison

nodes.label: Rank-based block decomposition (first/last index per rank)
nodes.rationale: Each rank computes N/world_size items starting at rank*n_per_rank; integer division drops the remainder so the last rank takes the slack, causing mild load imbalance
nodes.norm_label: rank-based block decomposition (first/last index per rank)

nodes.label: Per-rank memory allocation (memory split across nodes)
nodes.rationale: Each rank allocates only its slice, so MPI splits memory as well as compute, making very large problems tractable
nodes.norm_label: per-rank memory allocation (memory split across nodes)

nodes.label: Local vs global index pitfall (segfault)
nodes.rationale: After shrinking local arrays, loops still using global bounds read out of range; lower bound must be offset by rank to compute a unique portion

nodes.label: Manual master receive loop (rank 0 receives from each rank)
nodes.rationale: Non-root ranks MPI_Send their partial with tag 100+rank; rank 0 loops over neighbours with MPI_Recv; rank 0 does extra work and limits runtime
nodes.norm_label: manual master receive loop (rank 0 receives from each rank)

nodes.label: Replacing send/recv loop + bcast with MPI_Reduce then MPI_Allreduce
nodes.rationale: One collective replaces an if-branch of point-to-point calls and the follow-up broadcast
nodes.norm_label: replacing send/recv loop + bcast with mpi_reduce then mpi_allreduce

nodes.label: MPI reduction operators (MPI_SUM, MPI_MAX, MPI_MIN, MPI_PROD, logical)
nodes.rationale: No subtraction/division ops; sum negatives or product of reciprocals instead
nodes.norm_label: mpi reduction operators (mpi_sum, mpi_max, mpi_min, mpi_prod, logical)

nodes.label: MPI_Alltoall
nodes.rationale: Every rank sends an equal share to every other rank; useful when no master process role is wanted

nodes.label: Multi-node Slurm test (2 nodes, 8 tasks)
nodes.rationale: Running across nodes guarantees no shared memory, a real test that MPI communication is correct

nodes.label: Observed near-linear speedup (4 ranks ~1/4 time, 32 tasks 1200us to 42us)
nodes.norm_label: observed near-linear speedup (4 ranks ~1/4 time, 32 tasks 1200us to 42us)

nodes.label: MPI Makefile setup (mpic++, -lmpi, include paths, module load)
nodes.rationale: On the cluster, loading gcc and openmpi modules supplies include and library paths so only the compiler needs changing
nodes.norm_label: mpi makefile setup (mpic++, -lmpi, include paths, module load)
